summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic iron deficiency anemia, recurrent venous thromboembolism on anticoagulation, mild dementia, and chronic left chest pain was admitted for urinary retention with suprapubic pain. She had a Foley catheter placed in the ED with relief of symptoms. Workup revealed severe constipation as the likely cause, supported by MRI findings of chronic lumbar spine stenosis and nerve root contact. She received one unit of packed red blood cells for hemoglobin of 6.9 g/dL due to iron deficiency. Her INR was elevated at 5.5, prompting vitamin K administration; it trended down and warfarin was adjusted. She passed a voiding trial, remained stable, and was discharged home with instructions to continue iron, laxatives, and adjusted warfarin, with follow-up for anemia and anticoagulation management.
problems: Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Anticoagulants causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
